About Avtar Bani

The scripture at the heart of the Sant Nirankari Mission.

The book

Avtar Bani is the principal scripture of the Sant Nirankari Mission: 376 shabads (hymns) composed by Baba Avtar Singh Ji (1899–1969), the Mission's second Satguru, who received God-knowledge from his master, Baba Buta Singh Ji — a debt of gratitude that runs through nearly every verse.

Its one subject, returned to from every angle, is Nirankar — the Formless One, present in every particle, knowable not by ritual or scholarship but through the living True Master (Satguru) and a life lived in that awareness.

How to read it

Each shabad here is shown first in Roman transliteration of the original Punjabi, with the Devanagari (Punjabi–Hindi) line directly beneath each Roman line (Shabad 285 is in Hindi, as composed), then in its published English meaning.

Read the verse aloud if you can — the rhyme carries the teaching. Then sit with the meaning, and take the single line at the end into the day: into work, family, and the small decisions where, Avtar Bani insists, devotion is actually practised.

Words you will meet

A short glossary for the terms that recur across the shabads.

Nirankar
The Formless One — God without form, colour or limit, pervading every particle of creation.
Satguru
The True Master — the living teacher who reveals Nirankar and bestows God-knowledge.
Brahmgyan
God-knowledge — direct realisation of the Formless, as distinct from belief, ritual or book-learning.
Simran
Remembrance — holding Nirankar in awareness through the day, summed up in the words “Tu Hi Nirankar” (You alone are the Formless One).
Sangat
The holy congregation — the company of saints, whose fellowship Avtar Bani calls a refuge and a cleansing.
Hukam
The divine will or order — nothing, not a seed or a mountain, moves outside it.
Maya
The visible creation — the perishable world of forms that veils the Formless and deludes the mind.
Naam (Nam)
The Divine Name — its remembrance is the devotee's true wealth, and the means of crossing over.
Gurmukh
The Master-facing one — the devotee who faces the Satguru, accepts his word and lives by it.
Manmukh
The self-willed one — turned toward his own mind and Maya rather than the Master.

The Five Tenets

The Mission preaches and expects its followers to abide by these five tenets. They guide a soul through a journey of self-introspection, emptying it of every dimension of ego, vanity, illusion and hatred, and form the foundation for receiving Gyan.

1

The body, mind and worldly possessions are a blessing of God; and should be used as such, without having any ego or vanity because of these.

2

One should not have ego or vanity because of one's caste, creed, colour or race etc.

3

One should not discriminate or hate against anyone because of their food habits, dressing or lifestyle.

4

One should not renounce family life to become a recluse and be a burden on others. Rather, one should fulfil all responsibilities of family and society.

5

One must not divulge God Knowledge as bestowed through the True Master without the consent and blessings of the Master.

They act as moderators in times of excesses, tranquilizers in times of pain and mentors in times of illusion or fear.
